canonical_work: TRIDENT: Tri-modal Deepfake Perception, Detection, and Hallucination Grand Challenge
official_program_title: TRIDENT: Tri-modal Deepfake Perception, Detection, and Hallucination Challenge
formal_status: Listed in ACM Multimedia 2026 official technical programme for Nov 11, 2026; future-dated relative to 2026-10-12.
official_authors: Wen-Huang Cheng; Hong-Han Shuai; Khoa Doan; Hongxia Xie; Ling Lo; Jian-Yu Jiang-Lin; Kang-Yang Huang; Ling Zou
challenge_scope: Independent Image, Video, Audio tracks; TFQ/MCQ; Type-A artifact explanation on known manipulated content; Type-B authenticity plus reasoning on unknown content; macro-averaging within track.
reliability_metrics: Cover for annotated-artifact coverage; CHAIR for unsupported artifact claims among mapped claims; F0.5 prioritizes non-hallucination precision; TCS weights Detection 0.4, Hallucination Robustness 0.3, Perception 0.3.
empirical_summary: Official ACM abstract reports 21 registered teams and 99 submissions across tracks; states detection accuracy alone does not guarantee evidence grounding and winners combine specialist perception, evidence-guided MLLM reasoning, and unsupported-claim controls.
measurement_limitations: LLM maps free-text claims to a discrete artifact list; the accessible source did not show independent human calibration, IAA, causal evidence intervention, explanation stability, or appropriate-reliance testing. Treat as artifact grounding/hallucination, not causal faithfulness.
access_status: Official programme and organizer page accessible; indexed OpenReview excerpts available; direct forum/PDF in Chrome stops at browser verification; partial paper-text review only.
deduplication_decision: Reuse the single existing TRIDENT identity in 90 and rank-46 identity in 72; no duplicate candidate or ranking row. Add one transparent partial evidence review in 172.
